classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied enclosing-cube hint to identify four removable triangular corner pyramids, determine their bases and heights, and subtract their volumes symbolically.

content.prompt: A regular tetrahedron is a pyramid whose base and faces are all equilateral triangles. Find the volume of a regular tetrahedron if each edge has length $a$. Hint: The tetrahedron can be inscribed within a cube of edge length $\frac{a}{\sqrt{2}}$, as shown in the diagram below.

spec.description: Regular tetrahedron formed by four alternating vertices of an obliquely viewed cube. All six tetrahedron edges are retained; hidden edges use dashes.
spec.mathematics: Cube vertices A=(0,0,0), C=(s,s,0), F=(s,0,s), H=(0,s,s) form a regular tetrahedron with edge s√2=a.
spec.answerVisibility: No answer or additional measurements appear in the question figure.

answer.short:
$\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{2}}{12}a^3$ cubic units.

Subtract the four corner pyramids from the enclosing cube.
answer.worked:
Let the cube edge be $s=\frac{a}{\sqrt{2}}$. Each of the four corner pyramids has a right-triangular base of area $\frac12s^2$ and perpendicular height $s$.
$$\begin{align*}V_{\text{corner}}&=\frac13\left(\frac12s^2\right)s\\V_{\text{corner}}&=\frac16s^3\\V_{\text{tetrahedron}}&=s^3-4\left(\frac16s^3\right)\\V_{\text{tetrahedron}}&=\frac13s^3\\V_{\text{tetrahedron}}&=\frac13\left(\frac{a}{\sqrt2}\right)^3\\V_{\text{tetrahedron}}&=\frac{\sqrt2}{12}a^3.\end{align*}$$
